header.headline: Dividend Income Goal Calculator
header.subhead: Start with the dividend income you would like, then see how many shares it takes at a given dividend rate, and what those shares would cost.

goal.label: Dividend Income You Want, After Tax
goal.hint: Cash dividends only. Bonus shares are not counted.

cash.label: Cash Dividend Rate
cash.hint: 10% on ৳10 face value is ৳1 per share. Use the rate the company declared.

tax.label: Tax Deducted at Source
tax.hint: 15% is deducted from cash dividends before you receive them. You can change it.

price.label: Share Price (Optional)
price.hint: Add the price to see what these shares cost. Check QuickTrade Pro or the DSE.
price.dseLink: Check latest prices on the DSE

owned.label: Shares You Already Own (Optional)
owned.hint: Add what you hold to see how many more shares you need.

warnings.cash: Enter a cash dividend rate above zero.
warnings.face: Face value must be more than zero.
warnings.price: Enter a share price above zero to see the cost.

results.title: What It Would Take

caution.title: Dividends Are Not Promised
caution.body: Companies choose their dividend each year. It can be higher, lower or zero, and the share price can fall. This tool assumes the same dividend every year to show the arithmetic. It is not a forecast.

how.title: How the Goal Works

items.title: Turn the Goal Into a Year
items.body: A goal of ৳10,000 a month is ৳1,20,000 a year.

items.title: Find the Dividend Per Share
items.body: Face value × cash rate, less tax. ৳10 × 10% is ৳1, and after 15% tax you receive ৳0.85 per share.

items.title: Divide
items.body: Yearly goal ÷ dividend per share after tax. ৳1,20,000 ÷ ৳0.85 is about 1,41,177 shares.

how.example: Example: for ৳10,000 a month after tax from a 10% cash dividend, you need about 1,41,177 shares. At ৳100 a share they would cost about ৳1,41,17,700.

items.q: How many shares do I need to earn a monthly dividend income?
items.a: Divide your yearly goal by the cash dividend you receive per share after tax. The calculator does this and rounds up to whole shares.

items.q: Do companies pay dividends every month?
items.a: No. Companies on the DSE usually declare dividends once a year, so a monthly figure here is the yearly amount divided by 12, not a monthly payment.

items.q: Will the dividend stay the same every year?
items.a: Not necessarily. Each company decides its dividend every year, and it can pay more, less or nothing. Past dividends do not promise future ones.
No. This tool counts cash dividends only. Bonus shares add to your holding but are not cash. Use the Dividend Calculator to see both.

items.q: How much tax is taken from dividends?
items.a: The calculator uses 15% tax at source, which you can change. The company deducts it before you receive the dividend.

items.q: Is it wise to rely on one company for income?
items.a: Dividends can change or stop, and one company’s share price can fall. This tool uses a single dividend rate to keep the arithmetic simple. It does not suggest putting everything in one stock.
The yearly dividend per share divided by the share price. A ৳1 dividend on a ৳100 share is a 1% yield, before tax.

items.def: Money a company pays to shareholders, shown as a percentage of face value.
The nominal value of a share, usually ৳10. Dividends are a percentage of it.
Tax the company deducts from your dividend before paying you.
The yearly dividend per share divided by the share price.
The date a company uses to decide which shareholders receive the dividend.

legal: An estimate based on the numbers you enter, for education and information only. It assumes the same cash dividend every year, which companies do not promise. It does not include trading fees or charges. Share prices can fall as well as rise, dividends are not guaranteed, and you can lose some or all of the money you invest. This is not investment advice.
